notes: A one-repetition calibration pilot of cases 1, 4, 7, and 8 on 2026-08-24 was used only to refine grading observability; it is not a performance estimate and does not establish that these revised expectations pass. Cases 2, 3, 5, and 6 remain unrun. Grade critical source integrity and ontological correctness before aggregate quality. A capable baseline may produce fluent definitions, so compare semantic discrimination, provenance, workflow evidence, and resource use rather than surface polish alone. Web results are time-sensitive; record the run timestamp and verify every final URL independently.
metrics: atomic expectation pass rate: passed expectations divided by graded expectations
all-or-nothing case pass rate: cases in which every expectation passes
critical integrity pass: cases with every [CRITICAL] expectation passing
required-section compliance: final answers with all five numbered top-level sections in order
mandatory ISO/IEC 11179-4 compliance: singularity, positive declaration, descriptive phrase, no uncommon abbreviations, and no embedded definitions
genus quality: human score from 0 to 2 for immediate and ontologically correct superordination
differentia quality: human score from 0 to 2 for essential sibling-discriminating characteristics
ontological category correctness: human score from 0 to 2 for separating concepts from processes, artifacts, codes, fields, units, and value sets
reuse judgment: human score from 0 to 2 for evidence-supported Path A, B, or C selection
definition economy: human score from 0 to 2 for precision, independence, and concision
source claim coverage: attributed semantic claims supported by a cited destination divided by attributed semantic claims
verified citation rate: final cited destinations independently opened and semantically confirmed divided by final cited destinations
web-search actions and completed URL-specific retrieval actions
